title: ABISS: Evaluating Text-to-SQL Systems Through Agent Interaction
summary: Combines an eight-category taxonomy, council-filtered question generation and style-conditioned user simulation to separate diagnosis from final SQL/feedback quality. Oracle labels help, but clarification does not ensure correct SQL. Unanswerability is approximated by council failure, human auditing finds residual SQL-label errors, and simulated users remain cooperative. AIR counts termination after relevant feedback, not successful resolution.
artifact_status: Official project repository is a placeholder marked COMING SOON; runnable code and downloadable benchmark data were not verified released.

title: Learning to Clarify: Multi-turn Conversations with Action-Based Contrastive Self-Training
summary: ACT trains clarify-versus-answer behavior with action-contrast preferences and simulated multi-turn outcomes, improving small-data adaptation of Zephyr on AmbigSQL and two QA tasks. AmbigSQL pairs Spider requests with synthetic underspecification; its user simulator sees the target SQL, so reported recovery measures simulated clarification rather than human interaction.
artifact_status: Reference training code verified; the documented example uses PACIFIC, and a standalone AmbigSQL download was not verified. AmbigSQL is the benchmark introduced in this paper; it is distinct from the AmbiSQL interactive demonstration system.

title: Benchmarking and Improving Text-to-SQL Generation under Ambiguity
summary: Constructs two SQL references per question through four controlled Spider-schema perturbations. LogicalBeam varies join/selection plans and restricts template infilling to schema-name diversity, improving top-five coverage. Evaluation measures candidate availability against the constructed alternatives, not clarification-policy quality or selection of a real user's intended reading; gains and ablation effects vary by ambiguity type.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: AmbiSQL: Interactive Ambiguity Detection and Resolution for Text-to-SQL
publication_status: SIGMOD 2026 demonstration described in author manuscript; first preprint 2025
summary: Uses a seven-type taxonomy to detect ambiguity, collect multiple-choice or free-text clarification, maintain preferences and recheck rewritten questions before XiYan-SQL generation. The four-page demonstration provides 40 curated BIRD/TAG examples, not a controlled broad accuracy or user study. Repeated detection does not establish completeness, and the user-facing Abstain option skips a clarification rather than certifying request unanswerability.
artifact_status: Apache-2.0 code, frontend, and linked demo verified; live demo not exercised; standalone ambiguity dataset release not verified. Distinct from AmbigSQL in Learning to Clarify; current arXiv v2 has six authors and a demonstration-oriented abstract, unlike older indexed snippets.

title: AMBROSIA: A Benchmark for Parsing Ambiguous Questions into Database Queries
summary: Benchmarks scope, attachment and vague interpretations using human questions over constrained synthetic databases. Models receive complete schema/data dumps; best zero-shot interpretation recall is 30.7%, with only 1.9% AllFound. Resolved-input baselines reveal ordinary parsing difficulty. Evaluation flattens outputs to value sets, so matching is relaxed execution evidence; the benchmark does not test unanswerability or live clarification.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: Non-Programmers Can Label Programs Indirectly via Active Examples: A Case Study with Text-to-SQL
summary: APEL asks non-programmers to choose outputs on small, informative synthetic databases, then updates a distribution over candidate SQL programs. An 11-participant study on 240 Spider utterances improves annotation accuracy from 59% to 75% and reveals reference-label errors; candidate coverage and human interpretation remain limits, and downstream training gains were not evaluated.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: ARCS: Towards Precise Text-to-SQL via Structured Disambiguation
summary: Combines multiple-choice interpretation selection with numeric-threshold adjustment over six existing databases. Generated questions are author-curated and evaluated through a two-stage user simulator, separate disambiguation/SQL metrics and an eight-person interface study. Global conventions, annotation-relative coverage, non-empty intended outputs and permissive extra-column scoring bound the results; manuscript task counts are inconsistent.
artifact_status: Official TabulaFlow implementation and a public Hugging Face release with task files and SQLite databases are available. Dataset card declares CC BY 4.0; release and paper instance counts differ, so pin the selected snapshot. Artifacts were not executed.

title: BIRD-INTERACT: Re-imagining Text-to-SQL Evaluation for Large Language Models via Lens of Dynamic Interactions
summary: Evaluates 600 Full and 300 Lite tasks with ambiguity chains, dependent follow-ups, changing database state and a guarded user simulator. Models choose clarification and environment actions under budgets; success follows executable tests. Simulator-human alignment is measured across seven systems on 100 tasks. Ground-truth-informed replies, cumulative follow-up scoring and artificial costs bound generalization; simulator refusal is distinct from database unanswerability.
artifact_status: Code and dataset listings verified; not executed. Code MIT; dataset CC BY-SA 4.0. Full has 600 PostgreSQL tasks; Lite 300; Mini-Interact is a separate SQLite variant. BIRD-Interact-ADK offers modular agent, user-simulator, and database-environment services. Ground-truth solution, knowledge, and test fields are separated from public examples; use official evaluator access procedures.

title: What Is a Clarification? Estimating Model-Dependent Input Ambiguity
summary: Estimates model-accessible answer sets through answer–clarification–answer consistency. Four-model evaluation includes 96 AMBROSIA requests, with best set-F1 in two SQL settings; response-policy experiments are QA-only. Recovery shares a semantic judge with reference construction and can preserve confident errors. A singleton accessible answer does not establish that the user’s request has only one valid interpretation.
artifact_status: Full public preprint reviewed, including the SQL answer-set experiment and complete prompts. No official implementation or new dataset release independently verified; no experiments reproduced.

title: CLARITY: A Framework and Benchmark for Conversational Language Ambiguity and Unanswerability in Interactive NL2SQL Systems
summary: Generates SQL-grounded ambiguous and unanswerable questions with pivot-to-schema annotations, multiple facets and varied synthetic clarification responses. Evaluation separates binary detection, target localization and SQL recovery; the multi-turn task supplies a completed dialogue, so its results diagnose conversation-conditioned prediction rather than an agent’s live questioning policy.
artifact_status: Public generation code and Spider/BIRD-derived annotations, seeds, schemas and column catalogs are released. Executable databases are separate upstream dependencies; code is MIT and derived data is CC BY-SA 4.0. Release availability is distinct from reproduction of paper results.

title: CLEAR: A Parser-Independent Disambiguation Framework for NL2SQL
summary: Builds candidate schema mappings, collects multiple-choice selections and rewrites both question and schema for a downstream parser. CLAMBSQL adds ambiguity and clarification annotations, so the evaluation depends on those annotated choices rather than unconstrained conversations.
artifact_status: Publisher abstract was available in search; direct publisher page required browser verification. Author repository and dataset page were inspected; dataset page has files but no dataset card.

title: Disentangling Ambiguity from Instability in Large Language Models: A Clinical Text-to-SQL Case Study
summary: Decomposes interpretation/answer graph variation into ambiguity and conditional-instability scores. Controlled-interpretation experiments improve pooled failure prediction, but the generated-interpretation clinical setting shows no significant advantage over result entropy. Regime-based error concentration motivates clarification or review routing; actual intervention effectiveness and clinical safety are not evaluated, and results depend on generated interpretations and LLM judgments.
artifact_status: MIT implementation and examples verified; no standalone clinical dataset download verified; not executed. Repository includes offline similarity-matrix and live interpretation-generation examples; full-pipeline thresholds require domain-specific calibration.

title: Confidence Estimation for Error Detection in Text-to-SQL Systems
summary: Studies confidence-based rejection and calibration on English PAUQ distribution shifts and EHRSQL unanswerable requests. Selectors fit on a known portion of shifted data. Unsupported questions are often easier to reject than incorrect SQL for relevant requests, while compositional shifts cause substantial rejection of correct answers. Post-hoc calibration improves scores but does not remove this coverage cost.
artifact_status: Official artifact link inspected or linked by the primary source; no execution reproduced.

title: Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL in Large Language Models
summary: Compares verbal, consistency-based and token-probability confidence for generated SQL. SQL-Aware Confidence filters and folds syntax-related token alternatives; product aggregation leads on Spider while averaging leads on BIRD in the reported experiments. Execution feedback helps selected methods, but candidate-confidence calibration is not a guarantee of semantic correctness or a diagnosis of ambiguity and unanswerability.
artifact_status: No code or dataset release verified in this pass.

title: CoSQL: A Conversational Text-to-SQL Challenge Towards Cross-Domain Natural Language Interfaces to Databases
summary: Collects Wizard-of-Oz database dialogues with SQL, result descriptions, ambiguity and unsupported-request acts. Database-disjoint tasks evaluate SQL state tracking, successful-query response generation and user-act prediction. Tracking receives recorded clarifications after user affirmation; the paper explicitly leaves clarification-quality evaluation outside its tasks. Response BLEU and human logical correctness rank baselines differently.
artifact_status: Official project page verifies downloadable train/development data, baseline code link, and CC BY-SA 4.0 data license; test data withheld. About 3,000 dialogues over 200 databases; choose the relevant dialogue-act, response-generation, or SQL-grounding task rather than treating all turns as answerable SQL examples.

title: Data Ambiguity Strikes Back: How Documentation Improves GPT’s Text-to-SQL
summary: Studies value consistency, table coverage and row granularity using GPT-4 on 45 questions from two KaggleDBQA databases. Documentation and query clarifications are manually derived with reference-answer access, and benchmark answers are also corrected. Results support the value of explicit data semantics under this curated setup; they do not establish automatic documentation quality, broad transfer or a live clarification policy.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: DialSQL: Dialogue Based Structured Query Generation
summary: Detects possible SQL errors, asks multiple-choice validation questions and revises a black-box parser's query. WikiSQL experiments include reference-aware simulation and a separate 100-question human study; the latter shows a smaller gain than simulation. Single-table queries, predefined error categories and header-only context limit transfer. The author-linked repository is currently a README-only placeholder.
artifact_status: Paper links https://github.com/izzeddingur/DialSQL, but the current repository lists only README.md; executable implementation and reuse terms remain unverified.

title: Disambiguate First, Parse Later: Generating Interpretations for Ambiguity Resolution in Semantic Parsing
summary: Generates default natural-language readings, infills missing interpretations, then parses each into SQL. It improves reference-reading coverage over prompting and transfers across AmbiQT and AMBROSIA, but does not dominate in-domain fine-tuning on full coverage. Incorrect initial readings are retained, and the unambiguous evaluation does not penalize extra queries; coverage is not actual user-intent selection.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: DSABench: Benchmarking Source Discovery, Coordination, and Execution for Multi-Database Agents
summary: Provides 815 reviewed tasks for exact database-source selection, coordination and local execution, including 105 two-branch ambiguity tasks. One controlled clarification substantially improves branch-source recovery. Joint scores also include topology-label gates and corpus-specific comparators; retained wording/gold mismatches, only 22 sequential tasks and simulated dialogue limit broader capability conclusions.
artifact_status: No code or dataset release URL verified; unrelated PyPI dsabench package is not this benchmark.

title: Know What I don’t Know: Handling Ambiguous and Unanswerable Questions for Text-to-SQL
summary: Uses SQL-derived weak supervision to label problematic question spans, ground concepts and generate template explanations. Its six-category taxonomy is broader than NoisySP synthesis, which mainly creates column ambiguity and missing-column cases. Commercial evaluation uses failed requests; ordinary-query SQL tests are separate, and no complete clarification-to-SQL policy is established.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: Rethinking Text-to-SQL: Dynamic Multi-turn SQL Interaction for Real-world Database Exploration
summary: Evaluates SQL agents in dialogue with a simulated user and a mutable SQLite database, using final-state comparison and all-runs-success Pass^k. Tasks pursue a fixed, fully specified hidden objective through dynamic interaction; the paper reports full expert review but contains an unresolved total-versus-short/long count discrepancy, so neither perfect dataset correctness nor unrestricted intent evolution is established.
artifact_status: Official source, task-generation/evaluation paths and database-fetch instructions were previously verified; artifacts were not executed. The older repository name Real-World-SQL-Bench resolves to DySQL-Bench. The reviewed ACL 2026 paper reports full-scope expert review, but this does not prove error-free annotations; its headline and short/long task counts remain unreconciled.

title: EHRSQL: A Practical Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Electronic Health Records
summary: Builds temporal and cohort SQL tasks from hospital-staff questions over processed MIMIC-III/eICU data, with held-out unanswerable requests that can include ambiguity. Templates are shared across splits, and the strongest baseline uses the known unanswerable proportion. Time shifts, shuffled patient-associated records, synthetic costs and annotation assumptions limit clinical and cross-hospital interpretation.
artifact_status: Conference year is 2022 although the arXiv record starts in January 2023. Source paper links the official EHRSQL repository.

title: Overview of the EHRSQL 2024 Shared Task on Reliable Text-to-SQL Modeling on Electronic Health Records
summary: Compares eight clinical SQL-or-abstain systems on MIMIC-IV Demo, with unseen question templates and added unsupported requests. Reliability Score rewards correct answers/refusals and penalizes wrong attempts; all teams fall below abstain-all under its most severe penalty. Results concern the selected templates and ambiguity-reducing preprocessing, not clinical deployment readiness.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: EntSQL: A Benchmark for Grounding Text-to-SQL in Long-Context Enterprise Knowledge
summary: Evaluates SQL grounding in long-form business documents with 1,066 aligned Chinese-English examples from five domains in one enterprise. English experiments contrast schema-only, full-document and concise-evidence inputs; limited bilingual subsets and one-model error analysis bound transfer claims. Public databases and input JSON are listed, but gold answers are withheld; clarification and abstention policies are not evaluated.
artifact_status: Official Hugging Face release lists five SQLite database archives, bilingual JSON and evaluate.py. The card declares CC BY 4.0, withholds gold answers and describes a scoring platform under construction. Dataset viewer currently errors; archives were not downloaded and scoring was not reproduced.

title: Fundamental Challenges in Evaluating Text2SQL Solutions and Detecting Their Limitations
summary: Separates Text-to-SQL solution errors, benchmark-data defects and matching-metric biases, illustrating how ambiguity, missing schema information and false presuppositions distort evaluation. A multi-LLM disagreement heuristic supports manual Spider inspection; the resulting example lists are incomplete and do not constitute a validated automatic detector or production noise estimate.
artifact_status: No code or dataset release verified in this pass.

title: FALCON: A Model and Dataset Agnostic Framework for Synthetic Data Generation for NL2SQL Pairs
publication_status: Accepted to AKBC Workshop at EMNLP, according to arXiv comments
summary: Synthesizes SQLite question–SQL pairs using persona/reserved-word seeding, alignment filtering and optional alternative interpretations. Reported gains concentrate on harder queries, while synthetic-only training loses aggregate Spider accuracy; the ambiguity audit has high specificity but 28.6% recall, and cost savings are estimated rather than measured end to end.
artifact_status: Paper verified; public code or dataset artifact not located in manuscript links or targeted search. Distinct from the eosphoros-ai/Falcon Chinese enterprise benchmark.

title: Reasoning about Intent for Ambiguous Requests
summary: Trains models with DAPO to produce up to five interpretation–answer pairs, rewarding recall on ambiguous examples and precision on clear ones with ambiguity oversampling. Improves AMBROSIA coverage and transfers to AmbiQT. Human evaluation measures explanation–answer alignment, not correctness or user preference; over-generation, finite interpretation limits and simulated clarification comparisons remain important boundaries.
artifact_status: Training/evaluation code and linked model release verified; upstream datasets retain their own access conditions; not executed. Text-to-SQL model: https://huggingface.co/irisaparina/IntentRL-Ambig-Text2SQL-4B . AMBROSIA remains available through its controlled-access author download; do not mirror it.

title: LatentRefusal: Latent-Signal Refusal for Unanswerable Text-to-SQL Queries
summary: Uses a supervised TRGE probe over a frozen LLM’s intermediate activations to gate SQL generation. Experiments train separately for each benchmark and require white-box access; the SQL semantic-entropy baseline approximates equivalence syntactically. Reported probe overhead excludes the backbone pass, and refusal F1 does not certify admitted SQL correctness or zero-shot domain transfer.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: LinkAlign: Scalable Schema Linking for Real-World Large-Scale Multi-Database Text-to-SQL
summary: Separates database retrieval, irrelevant-schema filtering and table/column grounding, with pipeline and multi-agent variants. Its synthetic AmbiDB expands Spider with overlapping schemas while retaining clues for one intended database; this stresses automatic schema selection rather than live clarification, and gains vary across exact-match, location and recall metrics.
artifact_status: AmbiDB is described in the paper. The candidate Hugging Face dataset URL returned HTTP 401 during inspection, so a usable direct dataset release is not asserted.

title: Model-based Interactive Semantic Parsing: A Unified Framework and A Text-to-SQL Case Study
summary: Wraps a base parser with uncertainty-triggered yes/no questions and feedback-constrained decoding. WikiSQL and Spider simulations improve accuracy, but human results are smaller and metric-dependent: SQLova execution accuracy slightly decreases without additional information. A separate condition exposes gold SQL, so its stronger result should not be treated as ordinary user clarification.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: Evaluating and Enhancing LLMs for Multi-turn Text-to-SQL with Multiple Question Types
summary: Combines CoSQL-derived and generated conversations with four question types, and tests a selector/detector/decomposer/refiner framework. TDEX scores SQL execution on answerable or ambiguous turns and classification on other turns; response quality uses an LLM judge. Results concern a curated, imbalanced dialogue test, with numerical inconsistencies in some detailed reporting and no unrestricted real-user validation.
artifact_status: Code, train/test JSON paths, and CC BY 4.0 dataset card verified; not executed. Includes selector, detector, decomposer, and refiner agents, plus RQS and TDEX evaluation scripts; SQLite databases inherit upstream CoSQL access.

title: MultiSQL: A Schema-Integrated Context-Dependent Text2SQL Dataset with Diverse SQL Operations
summary: Extends CoSQL-derived dialogues with schema/content mutations and longer context, using GPT-4 generation followed by human correction. It introduces heuristic context-aware and database-state matching. History/refinement gains depend on model and operation, and Llama outputs receive GPT-3.5 extraction assistance. The fixed corpus tests state tracking rather than autonomous clarification or unanswerability decisions.
artifact_status: Dataset repository and database download link verified; README says evaluation code will be released, so code availability is unverified. Nearly 800 dialogue groups and more than 9,000 turns over 166 databases; distinguish fixed conversational context from dynamic user simulation.

title: Constructing an Interactive Natural Language Interface for Relational Databases
summary: Uses dependency parsing, schema/data mappings and user-verified query trees to translate complex requests into SQL, recomputing downstream interpretations after revised choices. A 14-participant, single-domain study improves task completion, but users still accept some wrong answers. Heuristic tree search, fixed condition order and timing restricted to successful tasks limit broader reliability and usability claims.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: ODUTQA-MDC: A Task for Open-Domain Underspecified Tabular QA with Multi-turn Dialogue-based Clarification
summary: Introduces a Chinese real-estate benchmark connecting SELECT/FROM/WHERE underspecification, table retrieval and clarification, plus MAIC-TQA. Its simulator provides canonical corrections only after matching gold detection labels, with optional paraphrasing; results show improved recovery of answerable targets under this controlled protocol, not general unrecoverable-answerability or human-dialogue performance.
artifact_status: Source directories, datasets, and launch instructions verified; not executed; repository license not verified. Paper reports 209 tables and 25,105 QA pairs; implementation includes scope validation, table retrieval, and SQL generation/validation agents.

title: Certified Against Which Oracle? Execution Labels Set the Reported Risk of Conformal Abstention for Text-to-SQL
summary: Crosses candidate-clustering and calibration oracles to audit marginal-risk abstention on Spider-Realistic. Suite-based labels change reported risk, while blinded expert judgments show that neither execution oracle is a semantic gold standard. Risk reduction mainly changes which questions are answered; schema-disjoint tests are empirical, and independent expert coverage is limited to two checkpoints at one seed.
artifact_status: Public analysis code and panel-results JSON verified in the official repository. Its current README lists additional pools and audit artifacts, extending the PDF’s older code-only availability statement; complete package reproduction was not performed.

title: ParSEval: Plan-aware Test Database Generation for SQL Equivalence Evaluation
summary: Generates small test databases from logical-plan coverage constraints using symbolic and hybrid solving. Pair-aware tests use both candidate and reference queries; reusable gold-only suites are a separate protocol. Experiments improve counterexample discovery, but NULL multiplicities, special functions and extra joins can escape testing. Passing finite tests does not prove unrestricted equivalence or validate the reference intent.
artifact_status: Official artifact link inspected or linked by the primary source; no execution reproduced.

title: “What Do You Mean by That?” A Parser-Independent Interactive Approach for Enhancing Text-to-SQL
summary: Aligns a question with a template-based restatement of predicted SQL, asks multiple-choice questions and rewrites the input for a black-box parser. Five-parser experiments include a 30-volunteer Spider study with smaller gains than simulation. The simulator uses reference-filtered options and searches answer combinations, so its results are idealized; candidate menus and supported rewriting rules constrain generality.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: Beyond Correctness: Resolving Underspecification in Agentic Text-to-SQL
summary: Externalizes planned clarification questions in a mutable pool that must be asked or explicitly dropped before SQL submission. It improves annotated ambiguity coverage with more questions, but does not always improve execution accuracy. BIRD subsets are filtered for solvability after oracle clarification, and groundedness counts questions mapped to annotated ambiguities rather than proving correct answer incorporation.
artifact_status: Paper and method description verified; public code or derived benchmark artifacts not located. Useful design reference for persistent clarification state and tracking silent assumptions.

title: PleaSQLarify: Visual Pragmatic Repair for Natural Language Database Querying
publication_status: CHI 2026 Main Track; acceptance stated on arXiv
summary: Clusters a fixed pool of generated SQL by output similarity and ranks interpretable feature decisions for visual clarification. AMBROSIA tests assume gold-consistent feedback; a twelve-person study uses SQL-familiar participants and small databases. Candidate-pool omissions limit recovery, and reported task completion credits partial subtasks rather than measuring exact original-intent success.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: PRACTIQ: A Practical Conversational Text-to-SQL dataset with Ambiguous and Unanswerable Queries
summary: Builds synthetic dialogues by mutating Spider schemas/values and reverse-generating user replies from target SQL. Baselines classify question types and generate SQL with supplied clarification, sometimes after the request changes. Missing-value unanswerability is a benchmark convention, not a rule for all empty results; scripted dialogue and inconsistent printed totals limit broader claims.
artifact_status: Official repository was archived on 2026-07-10 and documents a data-generation pipeline; a ready-to-use dataset download was not confirmed.

title: PremiseSQL: Evaluating Premise Critique and Abstention in Text-to-SQL Systems
summary: Pairs flawed queries with originals to measure premise critique and over-refusal under different prompts. Explicit flaw assertions improve detection while suppressing valid-query generation. GEN is coverage, with separate execution validation. Failure-mechanism analyses use selected consensus cases and AI-assisted human labels; they are not population-level causal explanations or evaluations of live clarification success.
artifact_status: Public MIT construction and evaluation code verified. The repository explicitly excludes source databases and the final paper dataset; a downloadable benchmark release was not verified. No code was executed.

title: QDA-SQL: Questions Enhanced Dialogue Augmentation for Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL
publication_status: CICAI 2026, according to updated arXiv and author repository; first preprint 2024
summary: Synthesizes multi-turn dialogues with answerable, ambiguous, unanswerable and non-database questions, then filters and formats them for intent routing and SQL generation. Mixed-type training improves recognition, but ambiguity/unanswerability F1 remains low in the displayed CoSQL experiment. AccS scores nonanswerable turns by category correctness, not clarification quality; absent-value cases are also labeled unanswerable.
artifact_status: Generation scripts, evaluation paths, and dataset directory verified; not executed. Supports schema-based generation and supplies a StateFlow-style inference example; MMSQL uses some QDA-SQL-generated data.

title: Query Carefully: Detecting the Unanswerables in Text-to-SQL Tasks
publication_status: HC@AIxIA + HYDRA 2025; acceptance stated on arXiv
summary: Adds schema-aware refusal rules and retrieved answerable/unanswerable examples to a biomedical SQL pipeline. Evaluation covers 99 OncoMX development questions and 80 synthetic, author-reviewed negatives; negative demonstrations are retrieved from that same pool excluding the current question. Balanced prompts help detection, but execution-error repair can increase wrong results and missing values or column ambiguity remain difficult.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: RAQS-SQL: Schema and Value Ambiguity Resolution in Text-to-SQL
summary: Combines question-to-column alignment with semantic and hierarchical value matching, and introduces AmbiVal from Spider and BIRD. The approach focuses on schema and value ambiguity; those grounding tasks should be distinguished from evaluating a full clarification dialogue.
artifact_status: Official code repository names the paper and DOI and exposes source/configuration/evaluation directories; code was not executed. The root source license was verified as MIT; vendored baselines, models and datasets have separate terms not verified in this check. Full article could not be read through the publisher verification gate or located in checked public alternatives.

title: ROSE: An Intent-Centered Evaluation Metric for NL2SQL
summary: Judges executable SQL with a Prover-Refuter cascade that treats reference SQL as challenge evidence and uses explicit acceptance rules for ambiguity. ROSE-VEC validates agreement on 585 expert-consensus cases; discarded disagreements, reference-visible human annotation and backbone-dependent diagnostic precision limit generalization. Observed leaderboard changes do not isolate model improvements from system engineering.
artifact_status: Public evaluator source and ROSE-VEC Spider/BIRD annotation files verified. No root license was identified in the inspected repository; underlying database access and reuse terms require separate checks. No experiments were reproduced.

title: Reliable Text-to-SQL with Adaptive Abstention
summary: Detects schema-linking branching tokens with hidden-state classifiers and conformal prediction, then abstains or seeks surrogate/human feedback. Linking and downstream SQL improve in tested settings, but guarantees concern marginal label-set coverage under calibration assumptions. Human help, hidden-state access and task-specific training are required; distribution shift and full-query semantic correctness are not guaranteed.
artifact_status: Official artifact link inspected or linked by the primary source; no execution reproduced.

title: Reliable End-to-End Text-to-SQL Generation
summary: RTS++ clusters candidate SQL by execution results and combines execution entropy with reranker scores for conformal calibration, abstention and user selection. Spider/BIRD results report accuracy on the non-abstained subset and assume accurate feedback. The stated prediction-set coverage should not be read as an unconditional semantic-error guarantee; candidate coverage, calibration validity and database-result normalization constrain interpretation.
artifact_status: Official artifact link inspected or linked by the primary source; no execution reproduced.

title: SCARE: A Benchmark for SQL Correction and Question Answerability Classification for Reliable EHR Question Answering
summary: Balances 4,200 question/candidate-SQL triples across correct, incorrect, ambiguous and unanswerable cases on three EHR schemas. It measures preservation, correction and input classification jointly; baseline prompts can include execution results and annotation evidence. Results expose model-dependent trade-offs, not execution-free verification, realistic clinical prevalence, completed clarification or deployment safety.
artifact_status: Public source and question/candidate-SQL records are present in the official repository. Underlying database downloads and access terms are separate; code and experiments were not executed.

title: What Predicts Correctness in Text-to-SQL? A Selective-Prediction Study
summary: Compares sampled agreement, model scores and verifier signals for selective SQL answering. Frozen judges and calibrated ensembles rank reference-execution correctness well on selected BIRD/Spider slices; trained verifiers transfer less well to held-out schemas. These are empirical, configuration-specific results. The notes flag abstract/table and figure/caption inconsistencies; calibrated abstention does not establish request answerability.
artifact_status: No code or dataset release verified in this pass.

title: Trajectory-Derived Confidence for Reliable, Resource-Aware Clinical Text-to-SQL Agents
publication_status: arXiv preprint; workshop acceptance reported by authors
summary: Learns per-agent confidence from execution trajectories to refuse, stop early or withhold final answers. EHRSQL utility improves at low error penalties, while higher-penalty results approach always refusing. Primary labels use an LLM judge, answerability has strong question-template shortcuts, and reported agent-step savings exclude monitor overhead; the study does not establish clinical deployment safety.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: SOMA-SQL: Resolving Multi-Source Ambiguity in NL-to-SQL via Synthetic Log and Execution Probing
summary: Uses candidate-SQL disagreement, an ambiguity taxonomy and executed probes to repair a selected query; optional synthetic-log clarifications supply extra grounding. Reported execution gains support the probing pipeline, but log experiments derive supervision from benchmark gold SQL without a clear disjointness protocol, and database evidence cannot by itself verify a user’s unstated intent.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: SParC: Cross-Domain Semantic Parsing in Context
summary: Provides SQL-expert-authored, goal-guided question sequences over disjoint train/test databases, with question-level and whole-interaction exact-set-match evaluation. Context-aware baselines improve, but later turns combine stronger contextual dependence with harder SQL. The corpus tests contextual interpretation, not agent-selected clarification, responsive users or abstention.
artifact_status: Official page verifies downloadable train/development data, baseline link, and CC BY-SA 4.0 data license; test data withheld. 4,298 question sequences with over 12,000 questions on 200 databases.

title: Sphinteract: Resolving Ambiguities in NL2SQL Through User Interaction
summary: Uses Summarize–Review–Ask to identify ambiguities and integrate clarification feedback into SQL. Benchmark gains use a gold-SQL-informed feedback oracle; the 11-person, SQL-familiar user study separates own-intent tasks from a second gold-visible phase. Reported gains are percentage-point changes, and neither simulator scores nor the gold-visible study establish novice deployment reliability.
artifact_status: Primary PDF reference format gives 2024; some citing papers use 2025. Repository includes experiment scripts and links to logs/user-study material.

title: Spider 2.0: Evaluating Language Models on Real-World Enterprise Text-to-SQL Workflows
summary: Benchmarks enterprise-style SQL workflows involving large schemas, multiple dialects, external definitions and dbt projects, with a tool-using Spider-Agent baseline. Workflow instructions can be underspecified relative to supplied context, but evaluation uses task-specific output checks rather than dedicated clarification or abstention metrics; Lite questions deliberately reduce ambiguity.
artifact_status: Official code, task variants, and data-access documentation verified; cloud access and execution not tested. Pin the specific Lite, Snow, or DBT release and evaluation setting; oracle-table access is explicitly a different condition.

title: SpotIt: Evaluating Text-to-SQL Evaluation with Formal Verification
summary: Extends bounded SQL equivalence checking with string/date support, backend-validated counterexamples and cross-system reuse. Finds differences missed by execution matching on BIRD and SQLite Spider 2.0. Such differences can expose incorrect predictions, flawed gold queries or valid alternative interpretations; bounded passes, unsupported queries and timeouts must remain distinct from proof of user-intent correctness.
artifact_status: Official artifact link inspected or linked by the primary source; no execution reproduced.

title: SpotIt+: Verification-based Text-to-SQL Evaluation with Database Constraints
summary: Combines mined database constraints, LLM filtering/repair and bounded SQL equivalence checking. BIRD experiments recheck execution-accepted query pairs under five-row bounds and set semantics; examples show how constraints change counterexamples. Realism remains best effort, users must validate domain assumptions, and neither bounded agreement nor agreement with a potentially faulty reference proves unrestricted correctness.
artifact_status: Official artifact link inspected or linked by the primary source; no execution reproduced.

title: Interactive Text-to-SQL via Expected Information Gain for Disambiguation
summary: Selects clarifications by expected entropy reduction over weighted SQL candidates, then filters candidates using feedback. Experiments use gold-based simulation and a confidence-filtered Spider subset. Results depend on candidate coverage and probabilities; one-step EIG does not establish universally optimal dialogue effort. The notes flag conflicting exact-match baselines and incomplete artifact/experiment specification.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: SQUAB: Evaluating LLM robustness to Ambiguous and Unanswerable Questions in Semantic Parsing
summary: Combines table-pattern detection, SQL transformations and LLM verbalization to generate ambiguity and refusal tests. Its evaluation is single-table; cost savings use estimated annotation costs. Out-of-scope unanswerability is not programmatically proved, and the small expert audit identifies category-specific failures. Generated tests therefore need semantic review before being treated as reliable evaluation labels.
artifact_status: Published PDF gives the named author repository; Anthology abstract still contains an anonymous URL. Repository is a generator, not proof that every evaluated dataset is publicly released.

title: Never the Number: Structural Abstention for AI Systems Whose Answers Are Consumed as Fact
summary: Proposes a generative shell around an authored, deterministic question-to-query kernel with user confirmation and refusal outside supported shapes. The report offers a qualitative deployment account and synthetic examples, not quantitative validation. Correctness remains conditional on authored mappings and meaningful confirmation; refusing an unsupported shape does not prove the request is intrinsically unanswerable.
artifact_status: Architecture/design report only; no code, schemas, datasets or quantitative performance artifacts supplied by the primary record.

title: TACO: A Benchmark for Open-Domain Text-to-SQL with Ambiguous and Cross-Database Queries
summary: Combines restricted smart-city examples and synthetic public-data queries to test table discovery and cross-database SQL planning. TACO-SQL rewrites requests without user confirmation; evaluation is single-turn execution agreement. Oracle-table and retrieved-table ablations differ, public release coverage differs from the paper total, and no all-interpretation or clarification-dialogue guarantee is established.
artifact_status: Public code and official linked dataset card verified; not downloaded or executed. Both repository and dataset card declare MIT. Paper describes 14,500 examples, while the current Hugging Face card reports 12,422 JSON examples and 46 SQLite databases; distinguish the described benchmark from the released snapshot.

title: Semantic Evaluation for Text-to-SQL with Distilled Test Suites
summary: Distills small database test suites that distinguish mutated neighbors of a reference query, improving evaluation beyond single-database agreement and exact-form matching. Tests approximate equivalence, not proof, and can miss prediction-only branches or unstated domain constraints. Historical comparisons substitute gold values; the 100-example human check covers selected metric disagreements, while Appendix A.3 documents a remaining false positive.
artifact_status: Official artifact link inspected or linked by the primary source; no execution reproduced.

title: Evaluating LLMs on Conversational Text-to-SQL under Chain Ambiguity and Intent Drift
summary: Pairs two-layer clarification chains and non-monotonic intent revisions over 514 BIRD anchors, yielding 1,542 samples. Metrics separate layer identification, structural drift and execution success. Drift recognition is an AST-change proxy, and the human audit retains residual validity failures. Results concern two-layer, chain-then-drift simulated dialogues; the linked repository remains a release placeholder.
artifact_status: Repository placeholder: only README, LICENSE, and .gitattributes visible; implementation and dataset not verified released. Name collision: this is the conversational SQL TIDE-Bench, not the unrelated tool-integrated-reasoning benchmark arXiv:2605.09544.

title: TraceSQL: Traceable Answerability Estimation for Reference-Free Text-to-SQL Verification
summary: Learns candidate-SQL verification from LLM-generated diagnostics and SQL-structure signals, retaining feature-to-evidence links. Held-out BIRD tests improve aggregate F1/AUC over GradeSQL-7B but reject many reference queries. The 67-feature pipeline uses reference-execution training labels and substantial upstream LLM assessment; traceability does not establish semantic correctness or general request answerability.
artifact_status: Paper verified; public implementation not located. Do not link the unrelated TraceSQL lineage product. Keep candidate correctness, input answerability, and calibrated deployment risk separate when comparing this verifier with refusal methods.

title: Did You Ask a Good Question? A Cross-Domain Question Intention Classification Benchmark for Text-to-SQL
summary: Classifies schema-question pairs into answerable, improper, missing-knowledge, ambiguous and Non-SQL categories using transformed corpora and a balanced, manually checked cross-schema test set. Non-SQL partly reflects the grammar supported by contemporary parsers, not absolute SQL impossibility. Evaluation concerns input triage only; SQL correctness and recovery dialogues are not tested.
artifact_status: Artifact execution and independent reproduction were not assessed.

title: TrustSQL: Benchmarking Text-to-SQL Reliability with Penalty-Based Scoring
summary: Evaluates correct SQL and abstention jointly with penalty-based scores on feasible/infeasible questions. Results depend on the chosen penalty and balanced test prevalence: abstain-all scores 50%, so coverage must accompany reliability. Ambiguity resolution is outside scope, and preprocessing removes empty-result cases and implicit context. A positive score is not evidence of deployment safety.
artifact_status: Distinct from the 2026 TRUST-SQL unknown-schema reinforcement-learning system.

title: Pervasive Annotation Errors Break Text-to-SQL Benchmarks and Leaderboards
summary: Uses an agent-assisted, human-adjudicated audit to identify annotation errors and ambiguity in dated BIRD Mini-Dev and public-gold Spider 2.0-Snow subsets. Re-evaluating 16 agent implementations on 100 corrected BIRD examples changes rankings. Corrections include questions, knowledge and some database rows; disclosed backend substitutions and subset coverage limit claims about current full leaderboards.
artifact_status: Official repository exposes code and data-access instructions; dependencies, downloads and reported results were not independently reproduced.

title: Bounded Semantic Planning and Deterministic Compilation for Reliable Enterprise Text-to-SQL
summary: Constrains an LLM to governed semantic choices and compiles paths, roles and grain deterministically. A small ACME comparison favors the complete system, but semantic knowledge, retries and development exposure differ from the DDL baseline. LLM adjudication, post-hoc exclusions, nonblocking undecidable checks and incomplete public evaluation artifacts limit guarantees and reproducibility.
artifact_status: A public reference implementation is linked, but the manuscript explicitly excludes benchmark questions, gold labels, fixtures, evaluation harness, frozen verdicts and traces from that snapshot. Exact campaign state and full end-to-end reproduction are unavailable from public artifacts.

title: Probing Ambiguity: Adversarial Intent Resolution for Robust Text-to-SQL
summary: Uses adversarial interpretation proposals, SQL execution and result-based pruning before generating contrastive clarification. Schema-only limits generation context, while verification still queries the full database. Benchmarks measure interpretation coverage, not user clarification quality or completed dialogue success; current-instance agreement can hide semantic differences, and reported serial API latency is substantial.
artifact_status: No official implementation or new dataset release verified in this pass; evaluated on existing AMBROSIA and AmbiQT benchmarks.

title: Building SQL Equivalence Proofs from Query Rewrite Rules
summary: Constructs replayable SQL-equivalence derivations by aligning logical plans and composing admitted rewrite rules. Positive results depend on rule soundness and schema constraints; replay checks the recorded derivation using the same implementations. UNKNOWN does not establish inequivalence. Coverage is measured on selected query-pair corpora, often labeled by execution agreement, rather than user-intent correctness.
artifact_status: Public manuscript inspected; no official implementation or downloadable evaluation corpus verified in this pass.

title: Developing and Benchmarking Verification Algorithms to Improve Text-to-SQL Generation
summary: Compares round-trip language critique and synthetic-database execution for reference-free candidate verification and selective abstention. Conservative combinations trade coverage and latency for fewer accepted errors. Benchmark audits use verifier-selected samples; table/prose and arithmetic inconsistencies in reported error estimates limit precise risk claims. These methods do not prove semantic correctness or distinguish every unanswerable request.
artifact_status: The proceedings paper supplies an artifact-availability link; downloadable contents and independent reproduction were not verified in this pass.

title: An OMOP-Based Open-Source Text-to-SQL Benchmark Dataset
summary: Evaluates OMOP SQL or exact abstention on concept-normalized inputs and a synthetic PostgreSQL database. The test mixes paraphrases of training-seen SQL variations with held-out variations, despite a stronger split claim elsewhere in the paper. High execution and reliability scores therefore concern this bounded protocol; raw entity linking, fully unseen-template transfer and clinical deployment safety are untested.
artifact_status: Official repository lists answerable/unanswerable inventories, train/validation/test files and evaluation scripts; not executed. README notes that split generation consumes the raw unanswerable list, while tagged versions are separate artifacts.

title: Schema-Free Text-to-SQL: Learning Enterprise Database Structure from Query Logs
summary: Mines query-log relationships and business entities for graph-based context retrieval in an internal enterprise study. Its public BEAVER evaluation instead reconstructs the graph from schema metadata. The reported 95.7% is execution validity, not answer accuracy; small-sample expert preferences and LLM rubric scores do not establish complete ambiguity resolution or abstention.
artifact_status: Public manuscript inspected; no official code or new dataset release verified. The public paper reports an enterprise study and a distinct schema-derived BEAVER adaptation; neither was reproduced.

title: Grounding LLMs for Database Exploration: Intent Scoping and Paraphrasing for Robust NL2SQL
summary: Combines in-scope/partial/out-of-scope classification with entity-preserving paraphrase augmentation. Component tests use constructed scope cases; search worsens BIRD scope detection, and augmentation helps BIRD/BI but not Spider. The paper leaves integration into a complete system handling complex joins/nesting to future work, so partial-scope detection is not evidence of successful interactive recovery.
artifact_status: Public proceedings paper inspected; no official code or dataset release verified in this pass.

title: AtomSQL: Interactive Disambiguation of NL-to-SQL via User-Guided Atom-Level Alignment
summary: Exposes disagreements between generated SQL candidates as clause-level atoms aligned with question phrases, then updates per-user preferences to rerank later candidates. The paper is an interface demonstration, not a controlled accuracy or user study. Resolution is limited to the supplied candidates, and its agreement-based scores are not established as calibrated confidence.
artifact_status: Public application, model-adapter and interface source files are visible. The demo was not executed, and no repository license was identified in the inspected file tree.

title: Same SQL, Different Decision: Aggregate Risk Hides Cross-Lingual Instability in Text-to-SQL Verification
summary: Audits English-calibrated execute/defer thresholds while holding SQL, schema and execution labels fixed across seven question languages. Aggregate risk can hide unsafe promotions and lost automation. Score transport restores coverage more easily than individual decisions; English pivot translation helps unevenly. Results are verifier/threshold-dependent and conditional on imperfect translations and instance-based labels, not end-to-end multilingual generation.
artifact_status: Official repository lists analysis code, candidate SQL, execution labels and verifier-score files. Artifacts were inspected by description and file inventory, not downloaded or independently reproduced; source datasets and model weights have separate terms.

title: Leveraging LLM-Generated Schema Descriptions for Unanswerable Question Detection in Clinical Data
summary: Predicts table relevance using LLM-written schema descriptions, a T5-small encoder and supervised relevance heads, then thresholds the maximum score before SQL generation. EHRSQL-2024 experiments keep the same 17 tables across splits. Description ablations improve detection, but unseen schemas, database-content-dependent answerability and downstream SQL correctness remain unvalidated.
artifact_status: The paper links venzino-han/ehr_schema_prediction, but both its GitHub page and API returned 404 on this check; public implementation availability is unverified. This does not establish that no implementation exists. No new dataset release or independent reproduction verified.

title: RAG-based Unanswerable Question Detection in Clinical Text-to-SQL
summary: RaQAD retrieves semantically similar examples for few-shot LLM prompts that classify whether clinical database questions are answerable, without additional model training. The institutional abstract reports clinical experiments and adaptation to schema changes. This supports inclusion as an answerability-screening method; detailed evaluation conditions, downstream SQL correctness and clarification behavior were not verified from full text.
artifact_status: Full-text audit remains blocked: author-linked ACM PDF returned 403; the institutional abstract supports the existing bounded summary only. No code/dataset release verified.

title: KODE: Mining Implicit Domain Knowledge from Historical Experience for Text-to-SQL
summary: Mines reusable domain rules from gaps between historical questions and SQL graphs, then applies retrieval, consensus and localized critique. Controlled studies show larger in-domain gains and smaller abstract-template transfer; optional memory backfill retains execution-based errors, so historical defaults and critic acceptance do not certify a new user’s intended semantics.
artifact_status: Public proceedings paper inspected; no official implementation or new dataset release verified. Execution-accuracy experiments do not establish live-user clarification or unanswerability detection.

title: LASSO: An LLM-Agent Synthesized System for SQL Validation
summary: Builds heuristic SQL test-data strategies through agent-assisted coding and human-reviewed regression tests. It refutes query pairs under sanitized, dialect-adjusted execution comparisons; survival is not equivalence proof. Some benchmark failures informed development, timing excludes external test execution, and the BEAVER unseen check measures non-empty generation for ten queries rather than NL-to-SQL accuracy.
artifact_status: Public GitLab source and test directories plus README verified via the project API. Experiment contents were not audited or run. No root repository license identified; the manuscript contains placeholder PVLDB citation fields, so venue publication is not inferred.

title: NL2SQL-BUGs: A Benchmark for Detecting Semantic Errors in NL2SQL Translation
summary: Benchmarks candidate-SQL correctness and a nine-category/31-subtype error taxonomy using screened BIRD references and expert annotations. Correctness labels primarily use current-database execution agreement, which can miss accidental matches. Its Type-Specific Accuracy is recall-like and does not penalize extra type predictions by itself; query answerability and clarification are separate tasks.
artifact_status: Official repository lists annotation JSON files, prompts and schema context. Database download is separate. No executable evaluation implementation or repository/data license was verified; files and results were not independently reproduced.

title: Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals
summary: Fourteen physicians prefer a conversational interface on MIMIC-IV Demo; pooled pilot/main logs show more clarification for freely composed questions. A post-study review judges 134/186 conversational SQL outputs correct (72.0%), despite high usability. This is not a matched accuracy comparison between interfaces; small-cohort, demo-database and designer-adjudication limits remain.
artifact_status: Full public manuscript reviewed. Dialogue logs and surveys are planned for release but currently available only on request with IRB approval; interface code and analysis scripts are request-only. No public implementation/log dataset verified and no study or model results reproduced.

title: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
summary: Studies requirement discovery and post-training delivery for one enterprise Oracle Text-to-SQL engagement using a fact-grounded simulated customer. It separates elicited facts, final handoff recovery and deployment gates; two of eight selected delivery configurations pass, but production compilation is not semantic accuracy and the discovery judge audit covers only 51 fact instances.
artifact_status: Public protocol and case-study limitations inspected; no standalone study code or dataset release verified. Referenced upstream models and SQL benchmarks are not new study artifacts.

title: SQLens: An End-to-End Framework for Error Detection and Correction in Text-to-SQL
summary: Combines database and LLM signals through weak supervision to diagnose clause-level errors and guide sequential SQL repairs. BIRD/Spider experiments report net fixes alongside regressions, with correction evaluated on syntactically valid candidates. Empty-result and schema heuristics can flag valid SQL; the system remains an asynchronous debugging aid, not an answerability or correctness guarantee.
artifact_status: Complete arXiv:2506.04494v1 author preprint reviewed, including Appendices A–F. Official NeurIPS PDF retrieval failed, so differences from the final proceedings version were not established. The preprint links an anonymous artifact; no complete public executable implementation or independent reproduction was verified.

title: When the Bottleneck Shifts: Diagnosing and Closing Information Gaps in Interactive Text-to-SQL
summary: Routes schema inspection, typed knowledge retrieval and clarification before SQL generation, with retry control and follow-up state carry. Reports 51.0% first-phase and 37.0% two-phase success on BIRD-Interact Lite. Gold-derived coverage is a diagnostic proxy; inconsistent budget totals and value-feedback case descriptions limit exact efficiency and equal-protocol comparisons.
artifact_status: Official source modules and archived trace filenames are visible. The website replays stored runs; live inference needs model services and upstream benchmark access. Code and experiments were not executed or reproduced.

title: Verifying Text-to-SQL Queries under Changing Business Semantics
summary: Revalidates fixed SQL against a requested business revision and knowledge cutoff using legal counterexample ledgers and exact monetary semantics. On 32 authored revision families, obligation coverage detects 137/144 discrepancies versus 127/144 for generic ordering; current-only and equal-weight scoring match, so revision-priority gains are unestablished. Evidence remains finite-suite, authored-schema and local-model scoped; no public artifact identifier is assigned.
artifact_status: Public manuscript and evaluation boundaries inspected. Appendix C states that no public artifact identifier has been assigned; no code or data release independently verified and no results reproduced.

title: Post-SQLFix: Property-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated SQL with Runtime Verification
summary: Uses static SQL diagnostics and explicit edit contracts to guide repairs, accepting only proposals that reduce violations and preserve monitored structure. It reports fewer residual execution errors than feedback-only repair; guarantees are bounded to the rule family, while full-pipeline accuracy gains and optional empty-result alignment must be distinguished from semantic correctness.
artifact_status: Current arXiv version and bounded-soundness definition inspected. Earlier OpenReview search results do not establish venue acceptance. No official implementation or dataset release verified; no experiments reproduced.

title: Text-to-SQL Models Make Choices Without Saying So
summary: Builds 204 controlled request triples on 12 existing databases to separate computing an interpretation from disclosing a calculation choice. Models often compute both specific versions but return one for the open request; deciding before separate generation and preserving wording improve coverage. Tests cover one choice/two references, score precision on clear requests, and use simulated users and reconstructed product baselines.
artifact_status: Official benchmark, scoring and method files are listed publicly; no data or experiments were downloaded or run. Repository describes a PVLDB paper, but an independent proceedings record was not verified, so publication status remains preprint.

title: Auditing and Repairing LLM-as-Judge Failures in a Production Text-to-SQL Pipeline
summary: Audits SQL-faithfulness judges using distinct enriched, random and active-disagreement samples, then compares replacements and selective routing. Unanimity gains apply to retained cases, and the Qwen–Opus accuracy comparison is inconclusive. One-domain gold and deferred data limit transfer/reproduction; unreconciled appendix cost and count arithmetic preclude treating precise savings or population estimates as established.
artifact_status: Official repository contains judge and analysis scripts; its README still defers the audit datasets despite the proceedings publication. The paper-described benchmark is not treated as a verified data download; no results reproduced.

title: SQLStructEval: Structural Evaluation of LLM Text-to-SQL Generation
summary: Measures canonical SQL-structure variation across repeated generations and input perturbations. A full JSON-to-SQL pipeline improves execution accuracy and correct-output concentration while increasing overall diversity. Metrics also reflect parse coverage; structural variation is not itself error. Selected error-case analyses are not population rates, and the notes flag an inconsistent COUNT(1) label in the pipeline illustration.
artifact_status: Official repository exposes core analysis, compilation and experiment files. Its README excludes sampled outputs, manually checked paraphrases, the DIN-SQL baseline and some scope-check components; code availability does not establish exact table reproduction. No linked code was executed.

title: The Consistency Hypothesis in Uncertainty Quantification for Large Language Models
summary: Formalizes and statistically tests whether agreement among sampled generations predicts correctness, including Spider, Spider-Realistic and BIRD, then evaluates similarity aggregation for confidence and selective generation. Support varies with model, dataset and similarity definition. SQL correctness is labeled by reference-result agreement on the supplied database; consistency is not a semantic proof or a diagnosis of request answerability.
artifact_status: Complete UAI 2025 publisher paper and supplementary material reviewed. No dedicated code or dataset release verified in this audit; no experiments reproduced.

title: SIMBA UQ: Similarity-Based Aggregation for Uncertainty Quantification in Large Language Models
summary: Learns confidence from similarities among sampled responses, optionally adding token-probability features. SQL experiments use reference-execution labels and random in-domain train/test splits on Spider, Spider-Realistic and BIRD. Calibration gains are stronger than selection/discrimination gains; matched sampling, labeled examples and untested distribution-shift behavior limit deployment claims.
artifact_status: Proceedings and method limitations verified; no dedicated Text-to-SQL implementation or dataset release verified in this pass.

title: Speak to your Parser: Interactive Text-to-SQL with Natural Language Feedback
summary: Pairs Spider parser errors with explanations and short human correction feedback to evaluate one-round parse repair. Correction uses exact set match; end-to-end scores are derived from initial successes and explanation-supported failures. The reported human ceiling estimates feedback completeness, not observed human SQL repair. Fully specified inputs distinguish this task from ambiguity detection and autonomous clarification.
artifact_status: Official repository lists train, dev, test and EditSQL feedback JSON files and declares CC BY-SA 4.0. It is a dataset release, not a verified release of the baseline models. Data were not downloaded or executed.

title: NL-EDIT: Correcting Semantic Parse Errors through Natural Language Interaction
summary: Predicts clause-level SQL edits from feedback, explanations and schema context, using synthetic pretraining and SPLASH. One-turn correction improves, but 16.93% of test examples gain errors. Its representation/evaluation ignores condition values and restricts subquery structure; structural progress does not guarantee semantic preservation or faster multi-turn convergence. Cross-parser gains decrease with stronger base parsers.
artifact_status: Official repository contains correction annotations, SQL edit/explanation utilities and data-synthesis scripts. A complete neural-model training/inference release and reuse license were not established from the checked inventory and README; no code or data was run.

title: Boundary-Aware NL2SQL: Integrating Reliability through Hybrid Reward and Data Synthesis
summary: Trains SQL generation, clarification, missing-constraint follow-up and refusal with mutated enterprise examples, supervised fine-tuning and task-specific reinforcement-learning rewards. Ent-SQL-Bench combines SQL execution agreement with LLM-judged natural-language responses. Evidence comes from a held-out portion of the authors' synthetic enterprise corpus; response-level clarification scores do not establish successful multi-turn resolution or transfer to unseen domains.
artifact_status: Official repository lists synthesis, training and evaluation scripts plus Ent-SQL-Bench.json. Required database access, model weights and exact reproduction were not verified. README declares MIT but no root LICENSE was listed; dataset-specific terms remain unverified.

title: Concept based Ambiguity Resolution in LLMs
summary: Uses sparse-autoencoder concepts and an approximate path-kernel distance between a question and generated interpretations to detect ambiguity in AMBROSIA-derived inputs. Generated interpretations serve as unambiguous controls, and a separate held-out threshold protocol is not clearly specified. The SQL evidence concerns detection; missing-concept prediction is evaluated separately on API retrieval, without SQL-generation or clarification-success results.
artifact_status: Complete public proceedings paper reviewed. No author implementation or new dataset release verified through the paper, proceedings links, author publication record and exact-title/identifier searches. AMBROSIA, Gorilla and cited pretrained sparse autoencoders are upstream resources, not new artifacts from this work. No code executed or results reproduced.

title: Node-Level Uncertainty Estimation in LLM-Generated SQL
summary: Labels generated SQL nodes by heuristic alignment with a reference AST, then predicts node errors from schema-aware features using LightGBM. BIRD and SynSQL transfer experiments improve aggregate ROC-AUC over token probabilities, with weaker out-of-distribution performance. Missing clauses receive no node label; calibration and downstream repair or selective execution are not evaluated.
artifact_status: Complete LREC proceedings paper and Appendix A reviewed. No official implementation or new annotation-data release verified through the paper, primary record and targeted author/title searches; no experiments reproduced.

title: SQLoom: Set-Contrastive Learning of Syntactic, Semantic, and Logical Dependencies for Text-to-SQL
summary: Uses parser checks and schema-legal counterexample databases to construct contrastive SQL training supervision, and reports correcting 378 Spider annotations including underspecified questions. Its relevance is verification-grounded supervision and label quality: query disagreement does not establish which interpretation satisfies a user, and reference/LLM checks remain assumptions. No clarification or abstention policy is evaluated; official code/data downloads were not verified.
artifact_status: The paper describes SQLoom and Spider-Refined as released, but no official implementation, checkpoint or dataset download was verified. The author publication page lists this work under Preprints and links the paper only. Exact-title and artifact searches did not establish a corresponding public release; the unrelated .NET project named sqloom is not this work. No code was executed or result reproduced.

title: From Textual Columns to Query Plans: A Unified Relational-Semantic Execution Framework for Hybrid Query Processing
publication_status: Findings of IJCNLP-AACL 2026; first preprint April 2026
summary: OmniTQA diversifies schema mappings and vague-predicate interpretations within plans that combine SQL and LLM operators over structured and textual data. It selects one answer and evaluates reference agreement; ACC@6 is an oracle candidate-coverage measure. The work supports ambiguity-aware grounding, without evaluating user clarification, abstention or exhaustive interpretation recovery.
artifact_status: Author-linked public source, notebook, README and BSD-3-Clause LICENSE inspected. The visible OmniTQA entry point executes candidate plans sequentially; the paper’s concurrent runtime and all benchmark settings were not independently reproduced. Upstream datasets are separate; no new OmniTQA dataset release is asserted.

title: Calibrating LLMs for Text-to-SQL Parsing by Leveraging Sub-clause Frequencies
summary: Combines token probability and syntactic sub-clause agreement across sampled SQL candidates using supervised multivariate Platt scaling. It improves aggregate calibration and error ranking in the tested Spider/BIRD settings, but requires labeled calibration data and additional generations. Scores concern candidate correctness, with an underspecified correctness evaluator; they do not establish request answerability or guaranteed abstention risk.
artifact_status: Complete proceedings paper and two-page responsible-research checklist reviewed. No paper-specific code, calibrated weights, generated-output bundle or new dataset release verified in the paper, arXiv record or inspected first/last-author publication pages. No linked code executed or experiments reproduced.

title: Policy-Conditioned Constrained Decoding for Column-Level Access Control in Text-to-SQL
summary: Masks disallowed column uses during SQL decoding and returns REFUSE for blocked or unsupported continuations. This is policy-conditioned refusal, not intrinsic unanswerability. Coverage counts compliant outputs rather than intent-correct answers; semantic execution is tested separately on permitted-reference queries. Guarantees concern a restricted single-query grammar, and token counts do not establish wall-clock efficiency.
artifact_status: Author-linked decoder, policy checks and evaluation source are public; MIT license text verified. The Spider-CU JSON was read in memory and contains 1,034 records across 20 databases: 684 SQL and 350 REFUSE labels. README declares CC BY-SA 4.0 for that derived file; upstream databases remain separate. README says BIRD-CU will be added later, despite the paper's broader release statement. Code was not executed and results were not reproduced.

title: Calibrated Interpretation: Confidence Estimation in Semantic Parsing
summary: Audits raw token and program confidence across semantic parsers, including Spider and CoSQL. SQL models appear more overconfident than dialogue parsers, while a separate Spider test-suite comparison reduces measured SQL overconfidence relative to exact matching. Teacher-forced token diagnostics, generated-sequence confidence and correctness metrics must remain distinct; clarification and safe-abstention policies are not evaluated.
artifact_status: Author-linked analysis/MISO code, SQL experiment branch and separate calibration-metric source inspected. Released EASY/HARD splits are SMCalFlow/TreeDST subsets, not new SQL benchmarks. No package installation, model execution or results reproduced; metric-package licensing is declared in metadata but its referenced LICENSE file was not present.

title: NL2SQL is a solved problem... Not!
publication_status: CIDR 2024; position paper with preliminary empirical studies
summary: Studies ambiguity and semantic mismatch in enterprise NL2SQL, including a two-annotator KaggleDBQA audit and questions paired with an unrelated database. Introduces Archerfish and a relaxed execution metric that permits selected output differences. Agreement is not ambiguity-detection accuracy, the mismatch test does not establish general answerability, and relaxed matching is not semantic equivalence.
artifact_status: Archerfish driver, adapters, result comparator, tests, workload examples and Apache-2.0 license inspected at a pinned public revision. No project code executed or results reproduced; no separately released ambiguity/answerability annotations verified.

title: The Case for Intent-Based Query Rewriting
summary: Proposes alternative SQL over available schemas when a query's original tables are inaccessible, allowing different results that raters consider useful for a similar analytical goal. Ten authored SQL queries and three-rater judgments test rewrite plausibility across 957 table schemas. Actual-data answer correctness and query-execution speed are not evaluated; correlated substitutes do not guarantee semantic equivalence or faithful recovery of the original request.
artifact_status: Official source and schema/example-resource listings verified at commit 61c48e36a7cd5cf81e7cd56257ef9631e572a861. README states user-study data were not uploaded, and main.py explicitly rejects natural-language input. No repository license was found in the complete 52-file tree; root LICENSE returned 404 and GitHub license metadata was null. The paper's license is not applied to the code. Database files were not downloaded; code and experiments were not executed.

title: Tracing Recurrent and Emergent Hallucination Patterns in Decomposed Text-to-SQL Generation
summary: Decomposes BIRD-mini SQL into executable sub-query paths and diagnoses six rule-based error categories across five models, with and without prior history. Separates categories recurring at the final step from those first detected there. Labels are reference-sensitive structural heuristics, not definitive semantic judgments; conditional recurrence is neither causal error propagation nor calibrated uncertainty, and no mitigation is tested.
artifact_status: Public decomposition/prompting and evaluation scripts, analysis notebooks, saved model outputs and heuristic annotations inspected at a pinned revision. Underlying databases are obtained separately from BIRD. No project code executed, results reproduced, or repository license verified.

title: MTSQL-R1: Towards Long-Horizon Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL via Agentic Training
summary: Trains a conversational SQL agent to execute candidates, retrieve earlier SQL and parsed constraints, and revise inconsistencies. CoSQL/SParC ablations support execution and memory checks; main results use gold history, with a separate predicted-history test. Verification remains a learned judgment with reference-based rewards, and clarification or unanswerability is not evaluated.
artifact_status: Official training, rollout, memory and reward source inspected at a720f970c4308980812d830bd60f1d69f2ab57fa. Four author-linked public model repositories list safetensors weights; weights were not downloaded or run. README requires locally prepared benchmark/parquet inputs; a separate trajectory-data release was not verified. Paper/source metric and verdict-tag discrepancies are documented in the reading note. No independent reproduction.

title: STRATOS: Bridging the Symbolic-to-Numeric Gap in Spatio-Temporal Text-to-SQL for Meteorological Data
summary: Grounds meteorological place names and fuzzy climate concepts through Wikidata/OpenStreetMap retrieval, a domain ontology and array-schema hints before SQL generation, then rewrites costly spatial predicates. Evaluation exposes valid aggregation interpretations rejected by single-gold result matching. Automatic grounding is not user clarification; exact and approximate spatial targets can yield different answers, and optimizer speedups depend on PostgreSQL.
artifact_status: The paper describes a system and evaluation workload; an official implementation or workload download was not established from the paper or checked public searches. No project code, datasets or experiments were executed or independently reproduced.

title: FlinkEval: A Synthetic Corpus for Evaluating Natural Language Interfaces to Streaming SQL
summary: Introduces a streaming-SQL corpus and a seven-level request-specification ladder, contrasting schema-explicit and potentially underspecified requests with ranked oracle clues. Reference-anchored and face-value model judgments diverge substantially. Clues are supplied rather than elicited through dialogue; per-item ambiguity is not validated, and judge-pass rates are not execution-equivalence accuracy.
